cards.explanation: The answer is that the kings came together to wage war against Joshua and Israel. Those were the kings of the Hittites, Amorites, Canaanites and the rest, from the hill country all the way to the coast. That's six different peoples gathered around one plan, friends, like a whole office actually showing up for the same meeting.

The answer is deceptively. The text says the people of Gibeon acted deceptively when they set out as envoys. The sacks, the wineskins, the sandals and the clothes were all part of the act, friends. They showed up dressed for a trip they never took.

The answer is False. The Gibeonites' whole supply of bread was dry and moldy. Fresh and soft would have ruined the look they were going for, friends. Even the stalest cookie I ever pressed would have been fresher than that sack.

The answer is that the men of Israel wonder if the Hivites live nearby. They say, “Perhaps you dwell near us. How can we make a treaty with you?” So they don't say yes right away, friends. They ask the question out loud.

The answer is because of the fame of the LORD. The Gibeonites tell Joshua they came “because of the fame of the LORD your God.” Keep in mind, bakers, this is the Gibeonites talking, and their story about a distant land isn't true. They make the LORD's name the headline of their speech.

The answer is False. The Gibeonites name Egypt, plus Sihon, king of Heshbon, and Og, king of Bashan, the two kings of the Amorites beyond the Jordan. Jericho and Ai are missing from the speech. Funny what a person leaves out when they're telling a story, friends.

The answer is journey. The Gibeonites say their clothes and sandals are “…worn out from our very long journey.” Cracked wineskins, patched sandals and threadbare clothes are what they wanted Joshua to see. The distance behind that picture was not true (Joshua 9:16). It's a very convincing look for a trip that never happened, friends.

The answer is that they did not seek the counsel of the LORD. The men of Israel sampled the provisions but did not seek the counsel of the LORD. They checked the bread and skipped asking Him, friends. Sometimes the thing we leave out is the whole story.

The answer is that Joshua makes a treaty of peace to let them live. Right before that, the men of Israel sampled the Gibeonites' provisions but did not seek the counsel of the LORD. The leaders of the congregation swore an oath to them too, friends. That treaty is going to matter.

The answer is True. The leaders of the congregation swore an oath to the Gibeonites, too. So the treaty had Joshua's agreement and the leaders' oath behind it, friends. Keep an eye on that oath, because it matters a lot.

The answer is False. Three days after the treaty, the Israelites learned that the Gibeonites were neighbors, living among them. The faraway land was a story they told, friends. A very long journey that ends up next door is quite a trip.

The answer is False. The Israelites did not attack the Gibeonites. The text gives the reason: the leaders had sworn an oath to them by the LORD, the God of Israel. The congregation grumbled against the leaders, friends, but no attack came.

The answer is that the leaders swore an oath to them by the LORD. The Israelites did not attack, “…because the leaders of the congregation had sworn an oath to them by the LORD, the God of Israel.” The oath was sworn by the LORD, friends. That's what stopped them at the gates.

The answer is wrath. The leaders say they will let the Gibeonites live, “…so that no wrath will fall on us because of the oath we swore to them.” They took the oath seriously, friends. They didn't want to break it.

The answer is that they will cut wood and carry water. The leaders say, “Let them live, but let them be woodcutters and water carriers for the whole congregation.” They keep their promise to let the Gibeonites live, friends. Wood and water are chores like laundry: finished today, needed again tomorrow.

The answer is a curse. Joshua asks the Gibeonites why they deceived him, since they said they lived far away when they lived right there among Israel. Then he says, "Now therefore you are under a curse…" (Joshua 9:23). He means it, friends, and the job that follows is a lasting one. I think this part is heavy.

The answer is that they greatly feared for their lives. The Gibeonites tell Joshua they were told the LORD commanded His servant Moses to give Israel all the land. So, in their words, “…we greatly feared for our lives because of you…” That fear is the reason they give for the trick, friends.

The answer is that Joshua delivers them so Israel doesn't kill them. Joshua delivered them from the hands of the Israelites, and they did not kill the Gibeonites. The congregation had grumbled earlier, friends, but the Gibeonites got through it alive. That's a hard outcome and a merciful one.

The answer is True. On that day Joshua made the Gibeonites woodcutters and water carriers for the congregation of the LORD and for the altar at the place He would choose. The work reaches all the way to the altar, friends. And the text says they're still at it to this day.
